query: W melts near 3422 °C, whereas Cu boils near 2562 °C, so conventional induction or arc-plasma casting cannot readily yield a uniform W–Cu material. Phase separation and void formation can impair thermal transport. Filling a W skeleton with molten Cu or Cu powder can leave defects; spark-plasma sintering and mechanical alloying can produce finer, more uniform structures but can also leave voids; vapor-coated W powders have been sintered to achieve near-perfect contact between the constituents; and metal 3D printing has also been explored. Starting from W particles or connected W regions within a Cu matrix for heat transfer under irradiation in fusion-reactor joints, what single intervention could overcome these limitations while preserving mechanical durability? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention and mechanism, predicts an outcome relative to a named existing fabrication baseline, defines the processing and service boundaries, cites supporting prior evidence, and specifies a controlled experiment and observations that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Spark plasma sintering (SPS) of mechanically alloyed (MA) W-Cu powders can produce a uniform and dense W-Cu material with improved thermal transport properties and mechanical durability.
generation.intervention: Mechanical alloying (MA) followed by spark plasma sintering (SPS)
generation.conditions: High-energy ball milling for MA, and high heating rates and direct heating of the powder for SPS
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a uniform and dense microstructure
generation.mechanism: Suppression of grain coarsening and elimination of voids and defects
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved thermal transport properties and mechanical durability compared to conventional casting or sintering methods
generation.boundary: Temperature range of 2000-2500 °C, and pressure range of 50-100 MPa
generation.uncertainty: The exact effect of MA and SPS parameters on the microstructure and properties of W-Cu alloys is not fully understood and requires further investigation

falsification_experiment.design: Comparative study of W-Cu alloys fabricated by MA-SPS and conventional casting or sintering methods
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the MA-SPS fabricated W-Cu alloy does not show improved thermal transport properties and mechanical durability compared to the conventional casting or sintering methods, the hypothesis is falsified

cited_evidence.text: This manuscript shows the study of the structure, mechanical, and chemical properties of high-entropy borides MeB2 (Me = Ti, Ta, Nb, Hf, Zr). High-entropy borides were synthesized by mechanical alloying and spark plasma sintering. A chemically homogeneous powder with a low iron content (0.12%) was obtained in a planetary mill by rotating the planetary disk/pots at 200–400 rpm and a processing time of 7.5 h. The structure, mechanical, and chemical properties of the resulting high-entropy borides have been studied. A single-phase hexagonal structure is formed during spark plasma sintering of mechanically alloyed powders at 2000 °C. The microhardness of the samples ranged from 1763 to 1959 HV. Gas-dynamic tests of the synthesized materials showed that an increase in the content of Zr and Hf in the composition increases the thermal-oxidative resistance of the material.

Casting [] and powder metallurgy [] are two common methods for preparing HEAs. For casting, there are two kinds of defects which are the vaporization of low melting-point elements and the elements segregation in the ingot []. For powder metallurgy, the HEAs can be prepared by MA and then consolidated. The HEAs powders prepared by MA are uniform and fine, and even form nanocrystalline. Hence a rapid sintering is needed to maintain this microstructure []. SPS is a new field-assisted sintering technique which can effectively suppress the grain coarsening by rapid heating and efficient densification in a few minutes [,,]. Compared with MA, gas atomization can produce more homogeneous powders. The preparation of HEAs powders by gas atomization is a rapid solidification process [], in which grain growth and element segregation are inhibited, and the high cooling rate even leads to the formation of an amorphous phase []. In the previous studies, two classical HEAs, CoCrFeNiMn with a single FCC phase and AlCoCrFeNi with a single BCC phase, have been extensively studied. A possible way to solve the problem of manufacturing Co-Cr-Cu-Fe-Ni HEAs that would exhibit a combination of excellent mechanical properties is to form the non-cast types of microstructure using alternative technologies for their production (e.g., the methods based on powder metallurgy). It has been demonstrated in refs. [,,] that single-phase CoCrCuxFeNi alloys having a nanocrystalline microstructure can be manufactured employing mechanically alloyed (MA) powder mixtures as starting materials and consolidation methods such as hot pressing (HP) or spark plasma sintering (SPS). The advantages of this technology over casting are as follows. Mechanical alloying can be used to produce solid solutions from metal powders due to high-energy mechanical impacts (multiple collisions with grinding bodies in the milling jars) despite the limitations or even the complete absence of mutual solubility []. The HP and SPS methods are used to consolidate powder materials at temperatures below the melting point of the main components. Therefore, the nanocrystalline microstructure inherited from the MA powders is preserved.

One way to enhance the reactivity of the powder mixture is to activate it by treatment in various apparatuses, mainly planetary mills []. The main difference from the above-mentioned mechanical alloying approach is that mechanical activation (MA) does not last as long and does not lead to the formation of new phases. During MA, the powders are crushed and the surfaces of the particles are cleaned from the oxide films. The contact area between components increases. Often, it allows the decreasing of the initiation temperature and promotes a more complete reaction in mixtures that burn weakly without activation []. Since Al-Co-Cr-Fe-Ni refers to systems in which SHS is difficult or impossible (depending on the composition), MA can be used to initiate a reaction in them without the use of a thermally coupled reaction. Moreover, preliminary activated powders can be used not only for combustion synthesis, but also for reaction sintering, which is based on the idea of simultaneous synthesis and compaction of the material.
